title: "The Region total doesn't match Excel"
seo: Power BI user acceptance testing drill: a tester reports that region totals don't match her Excel workbook. Reproduce the numbers, explain the difference and decide whether it's a defect or a requirement mismatch.
summary: Nina's UAT finding says the report's region totals don't match her Excel. Reproduce it, explain it and decide: defect or requirement mismatch?
impact: UAT is where the business decides whether to trust a report. Calling a definition difference a "bug" (or a real bug "by design") loses that trust for months.

messages.subject: UAT-017: Region totals wrong
body: Hi, testing the Q1 dashboard: West shows {{uat_sales_west|money0}} but my Excel says {{uat_home_west|money0}}. Central is the other way round. Europe matches. Total matches. Logged as a defect, severity high. Screenshot and my Excel attached.

evidence.title: Sales terminology (team wiki)
body: **Regions**: Sales are credited to the region of the store or rep that made the sale.

tasks: Reproduce both numbers from the data.
Explain the difference in one sentence.
Decide: defect, requirement mismatch, or test error, and record the UAT outcome.
Propose what the report should do so testers don't trip over it again.

deliverables.t: UAT log entry: test case, expected, actual, evidence, status, owner, notes

hints: Totals match and Europe matches; only US regions move between each other. Which two region columns exist, and which one did each side use?
Count orders where the sales region differs from the customer's home region.

rubric.good: Both sets of numbers rebuilt from the data, to the dollar.
Correctly classified as a requirement mismatch (two valid definitions), with the wiki as evidence.
Log entry complete: expected, actual, evidence, status, owner.
Nina's work is respected; the report gets a clearer label or a second view.

retro: How would the report's design have prevented this finding?
